findings.quote: names health insurers that depend on Obamacare subsidies as the clearest beneficiary of a House flip, with $XLV the liquid way to hold it
findings.why: Goldman's midterm note only lists ACA-exposed healthcare alongside defense and power infrastructure as policy-sensitive and says marketplace insurers have 'direct earnings exposure to ACA enrollment swings linked to subsidy litigation' with no direction; the long managed-care/ACA-credit call tied to a Democratic House is JPMorgan's D1 basket (JPMDC26P/JPMSC26P).
findings.fix: Credit the ACA-insurer beneficiary call to JPMorgan's midterm baskets, or restate Goldman's contribution as flagging ACA-exposed healthcare as a policy-sensitive area.

findings.quote: keeps the split outcome the base case
findings.why: The same JPMorgan note's betting-market table puts a Democratic House plus Democratic Senate at 47% against 39% for the Democratic House plus Republican Senate split, so the context's own odds make the sweep, not the split, the modal outcome, and House redistricting cannot bear on the Senate half anyway.
findings.fix: Drop the base-case assertion or replace it with the context's joint odds (47% sweep versus 39% split).
